Numeric eigenvalues used only for bound/interlacing display; integrality rests on exact ZZ factorisation (proof, not experiment). No essential inference or boundary error found.

originality.rationale: Compared delivered n<=8 log against nearest priors cited in topic.json: Bussemaker-Cvetkovic 13-graph integral classification (theory, no n<=8 polynomial logs or Hoffman residuals); Godsil-McKay switching (method, no minimal cubic witness log); Haemers-Spence / van Dam-Haemers enumeration to 12 vertices and MathWorld cospectral page (counts and quartic minimal regular pairs, no cubic-slice polynomial-plus-residual table); Hoffman bound paper (inequality, no census); OEIS A002851 / MathWorld Cubic Graph / House of Graphs (counts 1,2,5,19,85,509 and drawings, no certified spectra/verdicts/partition logs). Six of ten rows (K4, both n=6 cubics, Q3, Petersen-10, Heawood-14 spectra) are textbook-known values and not novel in isolation. However the four non-cube n=8 exact integer charpolys with ZZ-factorisations plus the unified Hoffman-residual and interlacing replay table for the 8-class slice is not shown to be published verbatim anywhere; counts alone do not mechanically imply spectra/integrality/residuals. Hence no prior result substantively contains the exact replayable log as claimed. Timestamp/failed-search alone not relied upon; substantive gap (no published polynomial+verdict+residual log for this slice) supports PASS on originality, with textbook overlap noted as value, not priority, defect.

value.rationale: Strongest self-contained headline actually delivered is an 8-class n<=8 census (not the admitted 621-class n<=14 census with smallest cospectral pair and Hoffman-gap table). Six of ten rows are textbook restatements: K4, K3,3, triangular prism, Q3, Petersen {3,1^5,(-2)^4}, Heawood (x-3)(x+3)(x^2-2)^6 spectra and their Hoffman tightness are classical. Only four n=8 non-integral polynomials are non-textbook, each an 8x8 integer determinant instantly reproducible by any CAS from the edge list. Scope n<=8 is explicitly tool-limited (n=10 timed out without nauty/geng) rather than the natural historic <=14 boundary; it captures only 4 of the 13 integral cubics so cannot cross-check the classification, and the fallback's smallest-pair witness is missing (proved absent <=8, minimum if any at n>=10 undelivered). The negative no-pair-at-n<=8 observation with 8 graphs is trivial once polynomials are computed and is already implied by broader cospectral enumerations (general graphs to 12 vertices; smallest regular pairs quartic). As a Ramanujan/integral benchmark or ratio-bound sharpness check the n<=8 table is too small to be reasonably needed later (cf. larger certified censuses at n=10-18). Certification is correct but does not rescue arbitrary truncation and missing substantive result. Hence independently not worth retrieving.
